scope: REQUIREMENTS.md Part A §1-4: the objective contract, trust and the provenance label, the gate, post-edit checks and receipts (packages/nana-pack) — 37 off-form origins split per design-ruling.md §2
notes: One merge found: R-050 ("shall be kept and enforced ... shall not police" is one promise stated twice, both halves proven by the same single existing test — splitting would hand the new row the origin's exact cite set, the sibling-cite failure shape the lane exists to catch). Every other extra `shall` is a distinct promise. New-row status defaults to 'untested' unless an existing cited test, read directly (never guessed from its title), independently and specifically pins that clause by an assertion that would fail if the clause broke; when in doubt, untested, per design-ruling.md §2. Revised after gpt-6-astra r1 BLOCK (batch-a1-astra-r1.md, 17 PINS/3 PARTIAL): R-763 and R-781 downgraded to untested (cited evidence covers only `read` / only the gate+objective, not the full promise); R-768 gained the subject-cap-exception cite that independently proves checking still runs; R-759, R-761 and R-794 flipped to implemented on astra-named existing assertions (T13 store-absent, hook-vs-pi equality, hostile-path receipt binding); R-760 flipped to violated recording objective.ts:479-480's obstructed-lock contradiction; R-764/R-771/R-783 reworded to stand alone.

merged.reason: "shall be kept and enforced" and "shall not police the owner's own regex" are the same observable promise stated from two directions (the one existing test — a catastrophic regex enforced as written — proves both at once); splitting would leave the second clause 'untested' on the exact same evidence the first already claims, the sibling-cite shape the lane is built to avoid
